confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on November 2026 web search results and converted them at about 1.10 USD per EUR. Inexpensive meal: about €13.50 (Numbeo, range €7–18). Mid-range meal for two without drinks: about €50 (Numbeo). Cappuccino: €1.80–2.04 (Numbeo, Expatistan). Bar beer: about €4.20–5.00 per 0.5 l (Expatistan, Numbeo). I did not find aggregated cocktail or wine data. Instead I used travel-guide ranges: craft cocktails €7–9, glasses of wine €4–7, and a spritz at about €4 average (Euronews index) to €7 in tourist aperitivo areas. Cocktail and wine are therefore less certain. The pricing window is July 2026, which is peak summer, so I set beer and coffee slightly above the cheapest local readings to allow for table service in tourist areas. The accommodation anchors are my own estimates from general knowledge of Sicilian summer demand. I did not search for or check any accommodation prices, so these are the least reliable anchors, especially the hotel_1star_2p value. The RBA rate came from a search summary that pointed to the RBA exchange-rates page and agreed with a secondary aggregator. I did not open the page directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: I priced Palermo as a large, lower-cost southern Italian city. Numbeo's comparison pages put restaurant prices about 24% below Rome and about 17% below Barcelona. Naples, Catania and Bari are similar. For July accommodation, I compared Palermo with mid-tier Mediterranean summer destinations in southern Italy.
